title: The Office - Interview Skills 4 - Talking About Work Experience
audio: mp3/244. The Office - Interview Skills 4 - Talking About Work Experience.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we have a new lesson in our series about interviewing for a new job.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们在我们的系列中有一个关于面试新工作的新课程。

segments.en: This is of course at the elementary level.
segments.zh: 这当然是初级水平。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So this is part four of our interview series.
segments.zh: 所以这是我们采访系列的第四部分。

segments.en: Remember we are taking a look each week at giving you tips and also the proper language for when you have an interview in English.
segments.zh: 请记住，当您接受英语面试时，我们每周都会为您提供提示以及适当的语言。

segments.en: And on this occasion we're going to talk about our work experience.
segments.zh: 在这个场合，我们将谈论我们的工作经验。

segments.en: Okay, you remember we talked a little bit about educational experience and educational background.
segments.zh: 好的，你还记得我们谈过一些关于教育经验和教育背景的事情。

segments.en: Well today is all about your last couple of jobs.
segments.zh: 好吧，今天是关于你最后几份工作。

segments.en: Alright, so I think we should just listen to the dialogue for the first time and we'll be back in a bit with language takeaway.
segments.zh: 好吧，我想我们应该先听一遍对话，稍后回来讲语言要点。

segments.en: Right Rebecca, now I see that after graduating from university your first job was...
segments.zh: 对，丽贝卡，现在我看到大学毕业后你的第一份工作是……

segments.en: For a local paper in York called the York Herald.
segments.zh: 是在约克一家名为《约克先驱报》的地方报社。

segments.en: Actually I started with them as an intern.
segments.zh: 其实我最初是在那里做实习生。

segments.en: I was really keen on getting some experience in journalism and this seemed like a good first step.
segments.zh: 我真的很想在新闻领域获得一些经验，这似乎是一个很好的第一步。

segments.en: Certainly.
segments.zh: 当然可以。

segments.en: And after your internship?
segments.zh: 那实习结束后呢？

segments.en: They seemed impressed and offered me a position as a junior local news reporter.
segments.zh: 他们似乎对我的表现印象不错，给了我一份初级地方新闻记者的工作。

segments.en: I ended up staying two years there actually.
segments.zh: 实际上，我最终在那里呆了两年。

segments.en: I was in charge of the sports news section of the newspaper.
segments.zh: 我负责报纸的体育新闻部分。

segments.en: I really enjoyed it there and it really helped me build my skills.
segments.zh: 我真的很喜欢那里，它真的帮助我建立了我的技能。

segments.en: Yes I see, but you decided to leave them in 2006, right?
segments.zh: 明白了，不过你在 2006 年决定离开那家报社，对吗？

segments.en: Yes that's right.
segments.zh: 是的，没错。

segments.en: My husband and I moved to London and so I managed to find a position with a national newspaper based in London.
segments.zh: 我丈夫和我搬到了伦敦，所以我设法在伦敦的一家全国性报纸上找到了一个职位。

segments.en: The London Weekly, right?
segments.zh: 伦敦周刊，对吧？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: In some ways it was a step down from my previous job but it did offer me much better prospects for the future.
segments.zh: 从某些方面说，新工作的职位比原来低了一些，但未来的发展前景要好得多。

segments.en: Alright we're back so now we've picked out a couple of key words and we're going to take a look at those now on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们回来了，所以现在我们已经挑选了几个关键词，我们将看看现在语言要点的那些。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: So Marco, a lot of people don't start out as a professional with a job.
segments.zh: 所以马可，很多人一开始并不是一个有工作的专业人士。

segments.en: They have something else first.
segments.zh: 他们首先有别的东西。

segments.en: What is this?
segments.zh: 这是什么？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: A very popular way to begin your work experience, you become an intern or you work as an intern.
segments.zh: 开始积累工作经验的一个常见方式，就是去当实习生，或者说做实习工作。

segments.en: Okay so the name of the job we could say is intern.
segments.zh: 好的，我们可以说的工作名称是实习生。

segments.en: I'm an intern or he's an intern at my company.
segments.zh: 我是实习生，或者他是我公司的实习生。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So usually interns work at a company.
segments.zh: 所以通常实习生在公司工作。

segments.en: Usually they're not paid or if they are it's a very, very little pay and the purpose of an internship or to work as an intern is to gain experience.
segments.zh: 通常他们没有报酬，即使有也少得可怜；而实习或当实习生的目的就是积累经验。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it's basically like a study opportunity for a job that you know you want.
segments.zh: 所以这基本上就像你知道自己想要的工作的学习机会。

segments.en: I could be an intern at a media company and I could learn all about media but it's not really a full job.
segments.zh: 我可以成为一家媒体公司的实习生，我可以了解所有关于媒体的知识，但这并不是一份完整的工作。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So it's really it serves as an opportunity to maybe continue working at that company in a full time job.
segments.zh: 因此，它确实是一个机会，可以继续在该公司从事全职工作。

segments.en: So you become an intern and the noun or what you are doing is called an internship.
segments.zh: 所以你成为 intern，而表示这件事的名词、也就是你正在做的事，叫 internship。

segments.en: So I'm an intern but what I have is an internship.
segments.zh: 所以我是实习生，但我拥有的是实习。

segments.en: It's like saying I have a job.
segments.zh: 这就像说我有工作。

segments.en: I have an internship but I am an intern.
segments.zh: 我有实习，但我是实习生。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Alright so we've covered those two words.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们已经涵盖了这两个词。

segments.en: Now let's move on to when she's describing her work experience in the York Herald and she described it as a very good first step.
segments.zh: 现在让我们继续介绍她在约克先驱报的工作经历，她将其描述为非常好的第一步。

segments.en: Okay so a first step you think about your foot, your step, your moving.
segments.zh: 好吧，说到 first step，你会想到你的脚、你的脚步、你的移动。

segments.en: It means the very first thing you do when you're heading in some direction.
segments.zh: 这意味着当你朝某个方向前进时，你会做的第一件事。

segments.en: Right and professionally I guess your first steps are maybe becoming an intern.
segments.zh: 正确而专业的，我想你的第一步可能是成为实习生。

segments.en: Right or you could say my first step was working in the mail room at this big movie studio but later I became a famous movie producer.
segments.zh: 是的，或者你可以说我的第一步是在这家大型电影制片厂的收发室工作，但后来我成为了一位著名的电影制片人。

segments.en: Exactly so that's kind of like the way that you begin your professional life.
segments.zh: 确切地说，这有点像你开始职业生活的方式。

segments.en: And well then they started talking about the newspapers and actually Rebecca was offered a position as a junior local news reporter.
segments.zh: 好吧，他们开始谈论报纸，实际上丽贝卡被提供了一个初级当地新闻记者的职位。

segments.en: Okay so junior means usually lower ranking or not experienced.
segments.zh: 好的，所以初级意味着通常较低的排名或没有经验。

segments.en: Someone who is just starting out and of course after junior we have senior.
segments.zh: 一个刚起步的人。当然，在 junior（初级）之后还有 senior（高级）。

segments.en: So a senior news reporter is someone who's worked for many many years as a reporter.
segments.zh: 因此，高级新闻记者是担任记者多年的人。

segments.en: Usually I guess a junior news reporter would make less money than a senior news reporter.
segments.zh: 通常我猜一个初级新闻记者会比高级新闻记者赚的钱更少。

segments.en: Exactly you could also say junior executive or senior executive.
segments.zh: 确切地说，您也可以说初级行政人员或高级管理人员。

segments.en: Junior manager.
segments.zh: 初级经理。

segments.en: These are ways of describing length of experience.
segments.zh: 这些是描述经验长度的方式。

segments.en: And in this case she's junior but what kind of job does she have?
segments.zh: 在这里她是初级职位，那她做的是什么样的工作？

segments.en: Well she is a news reporter for local issues.
segments.zh: 好吧，她是当地问题的新闻记者。

segments.en: Okay so she's a local news reporter.
segments.zh: 好吧，她是当地的新闻记者。

segments.en: Now what exactly does that mean if you're a local news reporter or for local issues?
segments.zh: 现在，如果您是当地新闻记者或本地问题，这究竟意味着什么？

segments.en: Well if I live in Chicago and I'm a local news reporter I only write or report the news about Chicago.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果我住在芝加哥并且我是当地新闻记者，我只写或报道有关芝加哥的新闻。

segments.en: It's a way of describing the things in my area.
segments.zh: 这是一种描述我所在地区事物的方式。

segments.en: So it's the opposite of our next phrase national news reporter.
segments.zh: 所以这与我们下一个短语“全国性新闻记者”相反。

segments.en: Okay so if you are a national news reporter or a national manager of maybe a company then that means that you oversee things in the whole country.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果你是全国性新闻记者，或者某家公司的全国经理，那就意味着你负责管理全国范围内的事务。

segments.en: That's right so local is my city or my county but in the case of national we're talking about the whole country.
segments.zh: 没错，local 指的是我的城市或我的郡县，而 national 说的是整个国家。

segments.en: Nation national.
segments.zh: 国家国家。

segments.en: So national is an adjective.
segments.zh: 所以 national 是个形容词。

segments.en: But we could even go further than this.
segments.zh: 但我们甚至可以走得更远。

segments.en: What if I am a reporter and I talk about foreign countries?
segments.zh: 如果我是一名记者，我谈论外国怎么办？

segments.en: I talk about France and South Africa and even Iceland.
segments.zh: 我谈论法国和南非甚至冰岛。

segments.en: Then I guess you would be an international news reporter.
segments.zh: 那我猜你会成为一名国际新闻记者。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And I guess also at the executive level you can have an international marketing manager right?
segments.zh: 我想在高管层面，你可以有一个国际营销经理，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: International marketing manager, national marketing manager.
segments.zh: 国际营销经理，全国营销经理。

segments.en: These are very important ways to divide work to say he is the international manager, he is the national manager.
segments.zh: 这些都是划分工作的重要方式：说他是国际经理，他是全国经理。

segments.en: This tells you the kind of the size of this person's job.
segments.zh: 这告诉你这个人的工作的大小。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Okay so now more or less you know how these jobs can be divided junior, senior, national, local, etc.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在你或多或少知道这些工作如何划分了：初级、高级、全国性、地方等等。

segments.en: So I think we should go back to the dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以我认为我们应该回到对话。

segments.en: Let's listen to this dialogue again and we'll be back in a bit.
segments.zh: 让我们再听一次这个对话，我们会回来的。

segments.en: Alright Rebecca, now I see that after graduating from university your first job was...
segments.zh: 好吧，丽贝卡，现在我看到大学毕业后你的第一份工作是……

segments.en: For a local paper in York called the York Herald.
segments.zh: 是在约克一家名为《约克先驱报》的地方报社。

segments.en: Actually I started with them as an intern.
segments.zh: 其实我最初是在那里做实习生。

segments.en: I was really keen on getting some experience in journalism and this seemed like a good first step.
segments.zh: 我真的很想在新闻领域获得一些经验，这似乎是一个很好的第一步。

segments.en: Certainly.
segments.zh: 当然可以。

segments.en: And after your internship?
segments.zh: 那实习结束后呢？

segments.en: They seemed impressed and offered me a position as a junior local news reporter.
segments.zh: 他们似乎对我的表现印象不错，给了我一份初级地方新闻记者的工作。

segments.en: I ended up staying two years there actually.
segments.zh: 实际上，我最终在那里呆了两年。

segments.en: I was in charge of the sports news section of the newspaper.
segments.zh: 我负责报纸的体育新闻部分。

segments.en: I really enjoyed it there and it really helped me build my skills.
segments.zh: 我真的很喜欢那里，它真的帮助我建立了我的技能。

segments.en: Yes I see.
segments.zh: 是的，我明白了。

segments.en: But you decided to leave them in 2006, right?
segments.zh: 但你决定在 2006 年离开那家报社，对吧？

segments.en: Yes that's right.
segments.zh: 是的，没错。

segments.en: My husband and I moved to London and so I managed to find a position with a national newspaper based in London.
segments.zh: 我丈夫和我搬到了伦敦，所以我设法在伦敦的一家全国性报纸上找到了一个职位。

segments.en: The London Weekly, right?
segments.zh: 伦敦周刊，对吧？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: In some ways it was a step down from my previous job but it did offer me much better prospects for the future.
segments.zh: 从某些方面说，新工作的职位比原来低了一些，但未来的发展前景要好得多。

segments.en: Alright so now let's start with a couple of phrases and phrasal verbs on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在让我们从关于流利表达的几个短语和短语动词开始。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: Okay in today's dialogue we heard a lot of really wonderful phrases Marco.
segments.zh: 好的，在今天的对话中，我们听到了很多非常棒的短语 Marco。

segments.en: Some of them are ways of making your experiences sound better, more professional even.
segments.zh: 其中一些是让您的体验听起来更好，甚至更专业的方式。

segments.en: For example this first one, sorry Rebecca is talking about her first job in York and she says I was in charge of the sports news section.
segments.zh: 例如第一个，Rebecca 在谈她在约克的第一份工作，她说我负责体育新闻版块。

segments.en: So that phrase, I was in charge of or to be in charge of, what does this describe?
segments.zh: 所以这句话，我负责或负责，这描述了什么？

segments.en: This describes responsibility.
segments.zh: 这描述了责任。

segments.en: Basically she's saying I was responsible for or I had to manage the sports news section.
segments.zh: 基本上她是说我负责，或者我必须管理体育新闻部分。

segments.en: She's taking credit for this job that was important.
segments.zh: 她为这份重要的工作赢得了荣誉。

segments.en: Okay so this is a key phrase because this is the typical phrase that you use to describe your responsibilities or to describe what you did in your previous job position or your previous job.
segments.zh: 好的，这是一个关键短语，因为这是您用来描述您的责任或描述您在以前的工作职位或以前的工作中所做的典型短语。

segments.en: So I could ask you when you were in marketing, what were you in charge of?
segments.zh: 所以我可以问你什么时候从事营销工作，你负责什么？

segments.en: Right and then you say well I was in charge of and then you explain your responsibilities or what you did.
segments.zh: 对，然后你说我负责，然后你解释你的责任或你做了什么。

segments.en: I was in charge of our national accounts or I was in charge of the local news.
segments.zh: 我负责全国性大客户，或者我负责本地新闻。

segments.en: Exactly so this is a very simple phrase, just remember it.
segments.zh: 确切地说，这是一个非常简单的短语，请记住它。

segments.en: I was in charge of and then you can start explaining what were your responsibilities, what you did in your previous job.
segments.zh: 我负责，然后你可以开始解释你的职责是什么，你在以前的工作中做了什么。

segments.en: Alright moving on now towards the end of that paragraph, Rebecca says that well being in charge of the sports news section was really fun and it really helped her build my skills.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在在那段结束时继续前进，丽贝卡说，负责体育新闻部分真的很有趣，这真的帮助她培养了我的技能。

segments.en: It really helped me build my skills.
segments.zh: 它真的帮助我建立了我的技能。

segments.en: So to build your skills or in this case I build my skills means that I have some skills but maybe they're not really developed.
segments.zh: 所以为了培养你的技能，或者在这种情况下，我培养我的技能意味着我有一些技能，但也许它们并没有真正发展。

segments.en: Maybe I just finished college, I want more experience.
segments.zh: 也许我刚读完大学，我想要更多的经验。

segments.en: Well in that time during my first job I build my skills.
segments.zh: 好吧，在我第一份工作的那段时间里，我培养了我的技能。

segments.en: I become better at writing or having interviews, things like that.
segments.zh: 我在写作或面试方面变得更好，诸如此类。

segments.en: Exactly so when you build your skills you kind of improve your abilities or you gain more experience.
segments.zh: 确切地说，当你建立你的技能时，你会提高你的能力或获得更多的经验。

segments.en: Another interesting phrase coming up here when Rebecca talked about moving to London with her husband she said I managed to find a position with a national newspaper.
segments.zh: 当丽贝卡谈到和她的丈夫搬到伦敦时，另一个有趣的短语在这里出现，她说我设法在一家全国性报纸上找到了一个职位。

segments.en: Okay so I managed to or you could say to manage to do something.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我设法了，或者你可以说设法做点什么。

segments.en: This is a really interesting phrase because it's another way of saying to be able to or to succeed at something.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的短语，因为它是另一种表达方式，能够或成功地完成某事。

segments.en: Okay so don't confuse it with manager or to manage people.
segments.zh: 好的，所以不要将其与经理混淆或管理人员。

segments.en: That is also correct, obviously it exists but to manage to do something is to as you said to be able to do something.
segments.zh: 这也是正确的，显然它存在，但设法做某事就像你所说的能够做某事。

segments.en: Right so for example I was running really late yesterday and I had a ticket for a train at five o'clock.
segments.zh: 对，比如昨天我时间特别赶，我有一张五点的火车票。

segments.en: I thought I would miss the train but I managed to get to the train on time.
segments.zh: 我以为我会错过火车，但我还是准时赶上了。

segments.en: That means I was able to get on the train on time.
segments.zh: 这意味着我能够准时上火车。

segments.en: Obviously so you managed to find a job, I managed to get to the train on time, I was able to.
segments.zh: 显然，所以你设法找到了一份工作，我设法准时上了火车，我能够做到。

segments.en: Alright and towards the end Rebecca talked about her job at the London Weekly and she described it as a step down from my previous job.
segments.zh: 好吧，到结尾时，丽贝卡谈到了她在《伦敦周刊》的工作，她说这比之前的工作差了一截。

segments.en: Okay is this a good thing or a bad thing Marco?
segments.zh: 好吧，这是好事还是坏事马可？

segments.en: To be a step down in something is a bad thing.
segments.zh: 说某件事是 a step down，意思是它变差了。

segments.en: It's to reduce in level or to decrease.
segments.zh: 是降低水平或减少。

segments.en: Okay so basically she's saying listen I had this really great job in York and I took a new job in London and the new job it wasn't as good in many ways because maybe she had less responsibility or maybe it paid less.
segments.zh: 好吧，基本上她是在说听我在约克有这份非常棒的工作，我在伦敦找到了一份新工作，而新工作在很多方面都没有那么好，因为也许她的责任较少，或者它的薪水更少。

segments.en: So this is a way of saying it wasn't as good as my last job.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种说它没有我上一份工作那么好的方式。

segments.en: Okay so her new job was a step down from her previous job.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以她的新工作比之前的工作差了一截。

segments.en: You could say I think his new girlfriend's a bit of a step down if you know what I mean.
segments.zh: 你可以说，如果你明白我的意思，我觉得他的新女友比前任差了点。

segments.en: So usually you're comparing right?
segments.zh: 所以通常你是在比较吧？

segments.en: You're making a comparison between something from the past to now.
segments.zh: 你正在比较从过去到现在的事物。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Okay so a step down.
segments.zh: 好的，所以 a step down 就是降了一级。

segments.en: Why don't we go back and listen to the dialogue for the very last time and we'll be back to talk to you in a bit.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不回去听对话最后一次，我们会回来和你谈谈。

segments.en: Right Rebecca now I see that after graduating from university your first job was...
segments.zh: 是的，丽贝卡，现在我看到大学毕业后你的第一份工作是...

segments.en: For a local paper in York called the York Herald.
segments.zh: 是在约克一家名为《约克先驱报》的地方报社。

segments.en: Actually I started with them as an intern.
segments.zh: 其实我最初是在那里做实习生。

segments.en: I was really keen on getting some experience in journalism and this seemed like a good first step.
segments.zh: 我真的很想在新闻领域获得一些经验，这似乎是一个很好的第一步。

segments.en: Certainly.
segments.zh: 当然可以。

segments.en: And after your internship?
segments.zh: 那实习结束后呢？

segments.en: They seemed impressed and offered me a position as a junior local news reporter.
segments.zh: 他们似乎对我的表现印象不错，给了我一份初级地方新闻记者的工作。

segments.en: I ended up staying two years there actually.
segments.zh: 实际上，我最终在那里呆了两年。

segments.en: I was in charge of the sports news section of the newspaper.
segments.zh: 我负责报纸的体育新闻部分。

segments.en: I really enjoyed it there and it really helped me build my skills.
segments.zh: 我真的很喜欢那里，它真的帮助我建立了我的技能。

segments.en: Yes I see but you decided to leave them in 2006 right?
segments.zh: 是的，我明白了，但你决定在 2006 年离开那家报社，对吧？

segments.en: Yes that's right.
segments.zh: 是的，没错。

segments.en: My husband and I moved to London and so I managed to find a position with a national newspaper based in London.
segments.zh: 我丈夫和我搬到了伦敦，所以我设法在伦敦的一家全国性报纸上找到了一个职位。

segments.en: The London Weekly right?
segments.zh: 伦敦周刊对吧？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: In some ways it was a step down from my previous job but it did offer me much better prospects for the future.
segments.zh: 从某些方面说，新工作的职位比原来低了一些，但未来的发展前景要好得多。

segments.en: Alright so talking about internships and interns it seems that usually it's not very exciting to become an intern because it ends up that the office people just make you make coffee or copies and stuff like that.
segments.zh: 好吧，说到实习和实习生，通常当实习生并不怎么令人兴奋，因为最后办公室里的人只是让你煮咖啡、复印文件之类的。

segments.en: You're not really gaining much work experience.
segments.zh: 你并没有真正获得太多的工作经验。

segments.en: That is the reputation in the United States for internships.
segments.zh: 这就是美国实习的声誉。

segments.en: So basically when you agree to do an internship, sometimes you have to apply to do an internship.
segments.zh: 所以基本上当你同意实习时，有时你必须申请实习。

segments.en: It's a very long process.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常漫长的过程。

segments.en: You end up like you say making coffee for people or photocopying reports and this is really boring work.
segments.zh: 你最终就像你说的为人们煮咖啡或复印报告一样，这真的很无聊。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: I think that is the reputation that many places have like you say in the United States but also I don't know I guess it does seem in a way the only opportunity in order to be able to get into an industry or a company.
segments.zh: 我认为这就是许多地方在美国的声誉，但我也不知道我想这似乎在某种程度上是能够进入行业或公司的唯一机会。

segments.en: Maybe it's a really good company like I don't know like Procter and Gamble.
segments.zh: 也许它是一家非常好的公司，比如……怎么说呢……宝洁（Procter and Gamble）那样的。

segments.en: And how else are you going to be able to get in there with no job experience?
segments.zh: 你还能如何在没有工作经验的情况下进入那里？

segments.en: Well that's right and a lot of people know that an internship doesn't really give you work experience but they still think that it gives you some edge or some advantage when you're looking for jobs later because if I write down on my resume, we were talking earlier about resumes, if I write down on my resume that I was an intern at Procter and Gamble, wow that's really impressive.
segments.zh: 好吧，确实如此。很多人都知道实习并不能真正给你工作经验，但他们仍然觉得，这会在你以后求职时给你一些优势。因为如果我在简历上写——我们之前聊过简历——如果我在简历上写我在宝洁（Procter and Gamble）当过实习生，哇，那可真是很拿得出手。

segments.en: Right, it looks good.
segments.zh: 没错，看起来不错。

segments.en: Alright so this is an interesting topic.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是一个有趣的话题。

segments.en: Let us know if you were ever an intern.
segments.zh: 如果你当过实习生，请告诉我们。

segments.en: Maybe you started out as an internship or maybe you're doing one now.
segments.zh: 也许你一开始就是实习生，也许你现在正在实习。

segments.en: Was it better than we say?
segments.zh: 比我们说的好吗？

segments.en: Did you do anything else other than making coffee?
segments.zh: 除了煮咖啡，你还做了什么吗？

segments.en: We really hope so and we look forward to hearing about your experiences.
segments.zh: 我们真的希望如此，我们期待听到您的经历。

segments.en: Alright we'll see everyone at EnglishPod.com and until next time.
segments.zh: 好的，我们会在 Englishpod.com 上见到每个人，直到下一次。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
